item.title: GovCon today: October 29, 2026 — SBIR's Free Ride Ends November 15th
item.description: SBA's new commercialization rule is the most consequential SBIR structural reform in a decade — and it lands as OTA consolidates around large integrators, DHS kills its pipeline forecast tool, and DoD's rapid OBBBA obligation rewards incumbents. The cumulative effect is a federal market quietly repricing small-business access upward across every major entry channel simultaneously. For small AI FFP shops, vehicle positioning is now a survival question.
item.content:encoded:
SBIR's Free Ride Ends November 15th

SBA's new commercialization rule is the most consequential SBIR structural reform in a decade — and it lands as OTA consolidates around large integrators, DHS kills its pipeline forecast tool, and DoD's rapid OBBBA obligation rewards incumbents. For small AI FFP shops, vehicle positioning is now a survival question.

item.title: GovCon today: October 28, 2026 — AI Evaluations Are Live — The Rules Aren't
item.description: Industry and legal experts are formally petitioning the FAR Council to set binding standards for AI use in bid evaluations — a gap exposed by the TRAX International Court of Federal Claims case and made urgent by the FAR overhaul's October 19th comment deadline. The governance vacuum isn't closing fast: formal rules are 18-24 months away at minimum, meaning the protest environment will be shaped by litigation before it's shaped by rulemaking. For small AI contractors, the move is to start building protest-record documentation now.
item.content:encoded:
AI Evaluations Are Live — The Rules Aren't

Industry and legal experts are formally petitioning the FAR Council to set binding standards for AI use in bid evaluations — a gap exposed by the TRAX International Court of Federal Claims case and made urgent by the FAR overhaul's October 19th comment deadline. The governance vacuum isn't closing fast: formal rules are 18-24 months away at minimum, meaning the protest environment will be shaped by litigation before it's shaped by rulemaking. For small AI contractors, the move is to start building protest-record documentation now.

item.title: GovCon today: October 27, 2026 — Gatekeeper Goes Live — And Closes the Door
item.description: The Army's Project Gatekeeper launched Friday, automating the ATO process that has historically taken months — but the consensus that this is unambiguously good for small vendors is wrong. Gatekeeper rewards architectures already designed for automated compliance, and the Army's plan to integrate frontier AI models into the authorization pipeline creates a path-of-least-resistance that favors large incumbents. For a small FFP-preferring AI shop, the compliance barrier hasn't been removed — it's been moved earlier in the acquisition timeline, before the solicitation drops.

item.content:encoded:
Pentagon Turns Political AI Directives Into Contract Law

The Defense Department's new ideological neutrality guidance for AI procurement isn't political noise — it's a signed memorandum with mandatory compliance teeth, standardized contract language, and a new audit surface that creates real performance risk on firm-fixed-price work. For small AI shops with auditable, domestically-trained models, this guidance is a differentiator, not a burden. Meanwhile, the federal AI market is bifurcating: sole-source incumbents at the foundation-model layer, a crowded commercial marketplace below — and three agencies are each trying to impose order on the same broken architecture without coordinating.

item.content:encoded:
DISA's Sole-Source Trap and the Selection Filter

The federal government is simultaneously signaling openness to new vendors and systematically locking them out — and today's DISA Enclave protest makes the mechanism explicit. A small SDVOSB is challenging DISA's sole-source expansion to Leidos after the agency abandoned a small-business sources sought notice, sat on the requirement for three years, and then invoked deadline pressure to justify skipping competition. The broader pattern: AI governance hardening, defense tech M&A, and compressed agency timelines are all narrowing the funnel — in ways that favor clean-provenance U.S. AI shops that know how to protest.

item.content:encoded:
War Force and the Insourcing Bet

DoD's 'War Force' initiative — offering two-year AI and software engineering tours at up to $200K — is not just a talent competition story. It is a structural insourcing bet that, if it works, reduces demand for the bounded, outcome-defined AI work that small FFP contractors do best. Paired with the CIA's internal tech restructuring and eroding DOT&E testing capacity, this week's pattern is a coherent institutional strategy to route around the acquisition system for core AI capability. Small AI shops need to move upmarket toward contractor-specific IP and clearance-plus-expertise combinations the government genuinely cannot self-perform.

item.content:encoded:

FedRAMP's finalized 2026 consolidated rules make 20x certification broadly available as of July 4th and mandatory by January 1st, 2027 — the single most consequential near-term authorization change for small AI-as-a-service firms selling to DoD and VA. Today's episode closes the compliance-as-moat arc tracked all week and maps the trifecta — FedRAMP 20x, the OMB PQC mandate, and operational AI fielding — into a coherent near-term procurement picture for FFP-preferring AI shops.

item.content:encoded:
GSA Writes the AI Compliance Rulebook

GSA has proposed the first AI-specific acquisition clause in federal contracting history, imposing a four-role taxonomy — developer, operator, integrator, service provider — with distinct flow-down requirements on every GSA vehicle prime. The rule lands on top of an open FAR comment window, compressing the timeline in which small AI contractors must engage on both foundational procurement reform and new AI-specific compliance requirements simultaneously. item.title: GovCon today: June 23, 2026 — GAO on the Chopping Block
item.description: The FAR overhaul's 1,000-plus pages hit the Federal Register this week, and the most consequential provision isn't the plain-language rewrite — it's the Part 33 proposal to strip GAO of bid protest jurisdiction and move it inside procuring agencies. For small FFP-preferring AI contractors, GAO is the last independent check on large-incumbent wins; losing it while prime consolidation accelerates is a structural double hit. The comment window is open now, and a sparse record is a gift to the provision's proponents.
item.content:encoded:
GAO on the Chopping Block

The FAR overhaul's 1,000-plus pages hit the Federal Register this week, and the most consequential provision isn't the plain-language rewrite — it's the Part 33 proposal to strip GAO of bid protest jurisdiction and move it inside procuring agencies. For small FFP-preferring AI contractors, GAO is the last independent check on large-incumbent wins; losing it while prime consolidation accelerates is a structural double hit. The comment window is open now, and a sparse record is a gift to the provision's proponents.
